- [RCTS.1.2.30] **`expect.expected_pump_statuses`** (optional,
  `adapter_calls`, `replay_determinism`, `cross_tier_fact_counts` and
  `cross_tier_per_engine_event_counts` only) — an array of integers, one for each `pump` step of
  `steps`, in order: `0` for a pump the runtime completes with no error, and
  otherwise the status the pump reports: the negative integer a
  `runtime_error` fixture's `code` carries for it, as a number and not a
  string ([RCTS.1.2.25]). In a cross-tier fixture ([RCTS.1.2.29]) the `pump`
  steps are every engine's, in the order of `steps`, and each entry is the
  status of the engine its step names. With the field, a pump
  the runtime refuses is not a refused step ([RCTS.1.2.28]): a harness must
  compare its status with its entry and go on to the next step. A harness
  must fail the fixture when the array's length is not the number of `pump`
  steps, or when a pump's status is not its entry. Without the field, a pump
  the runtime refuses fails the fixture ([RCTS.1.2.28]).

  On a `replay_determinism` fixture the field states the recorded run's pumps,
  a status a replay continues past ([RFCS.6.7]). The replay is judged as without
  the field. Such a fixture carries no `tamper`, whose run ends at the step that
  halts it ([RCTS.1.2.21]).

  A harness must fail a fixture whose `expected_pump_statuses` is not an
  array of integers each `0` or less, a `replay_determinism` fixture that
  carries both it and `tamper`, and a fixture of any other `expect.kind` that
  carries the field.
